banner.title: Play the buggy game
banner.now: Start the game and let one enemy shot reach the ship.

callout.title: This build has a bug
items: The first enemy hit destroys the ship, even with three lives left.
callout.hidden: One more defect hides in this build. The first loop cannot see it yet; the second loop finds it.

stages.after: When the run ends, the HUD still shows lives left. That gap between the rules and the game is what the loop starts from.

banner.title: Map the code before touching it
banner.now: Read the map: four source files and no tests.

badge.reason: Reading and summarising a small codebase needs breadth, not deep reasoning.

session.summary: Sky Sentinel is a small canvas shooter: a game loop, a damage handler, a hazards module, and a renderer. Nothing is tested automatically; behaviour is checked by playing.

sections.heading: Map
items: src/game.js runs the loop: input, movement, collisions, then rendering, 60 times a second.
src/damage.js decides what a hit does to the ship.
src/hazards.js moves asteroids and runs timed hazards.
src/render.js draws the frame; it reads state and never changes it.

sections.heading: What the reader should know first
items: Every rule about lives lives in src/damage.js, so a damage bug starts there.
There is no tests/ folder yet.

banner.title: Find the first bug, with evidence
banner.now: Read the finding and the reproduction, then the note on what the review could not check.

badge.reason: Judging behaviour against the rules and proving it with a reproduction is the step where a weaker model misses things.

session.summary: One confirmed defect: a hit ignores lives. Seeded runs end at the first hit, with all three lives still showing.

sections.heading: Finding P1: the first hit destroys the ship
items: applyEnemyHit returns destroyed: true for every hit and never reads ship.lives.
The design says a hit costs one life, with a short invulnerability window after it.

code.label: src/damage.js, lines 2-5

checks.name: seed 4242: first hit at 8.5 s, ship destroyed, lives shown 3
seed 7: first hit at 11.2 s, ship destroyed, lives shown 3
seed 90210: first hit at 9.8 s, ship destroyed, lives shown 3

sections.heading: Not checked
items: Every run ended at the first hit, before 13 seconds. Nothing that happens later in a run was observed.

banner.title: Turn the finding into a plan
banner.now: Check the three phases and the definition of done.

badge.reason: Sequencing a fix with its tests and release needs care, but the problem is already understood.

session.summary: Plan v1.0.1 has three phases, each ending in one local commit; only the last one publishes.

sections.heading: Goal
items: A hit costs one life and gives 120 ticks of invulnerability; the last life ends the run.

sections.heading: Phases
items: 1. Fix applyEnemyHit to count lives and add the invulnerability window.
2. Add unit tests for one hit, a hit during invulnerability, and the last life.
3. Update the changelog and release v1.0.1.

sections.heading: Definition of done
items: The three seeded reproductions from the review survive their first hit.
The new tests pass, and the full suite stays green.

## Phase 2: Unit tests for damage
## Phase 3: Changelog and release

badge.reason: A small, well-specified change in one file; the plan already settled the hard questions.

session.summary: Phase 1 is done: applyEnemyHit counts lives and starts the invulnerability window. Lint and build pass.

banner.title: Prove the fix with tests
banner.now: Read the three tests and their results.

badge.reason: Writing unit tests for a small pure function is routine once the rules are written down.

session.summary: Three unit tests now pin the damage rules. All pass, and the suite runs in under a second.

sections.heading: Tests added
items: A hit costs one life, not the ship.
A hit during invulnerability costs nothing.
The last life ends the run.

banner.now: Read the changelog entry, then play the new build.

callout.title: One bug fixed, one still hiding
items: A hit now costs one life, as it should.
Play long enough: the ship sometimes explodes with nothing touching it.

stages.after: The first review could not see this: every run it watched ended at the first hit, before the hidden bug had time to fire.

banner.title: Review again, with longer runs
banner.now: Read the new finding and why the first review missed it.

badge.reason: An intermittent defect that appears only after 20 seconds needs the most careful reasoning and the most evidence.

session.summary: One new confirmed defect: a leftover self-test in src/hazards.js destroys the ship at random after 20 seconds of play.

sections.heading: Finding P1: random explosions with no hit
items: tickHazards still runs a self-test from the debris prototype: after tick 1,200 it blows the ship up with a small chance every tick.
The comment says it was meant to be removed before release.

sections.heading: Why loop 1 missed it
items: The first-hit bug ended every observed run before 13 seconds, so the self-test never had time to fire.

banner.title: A smaller plan for a smaller fix
banner.now: Check the two phases and the test that must stay green.

badge.reason: The cause is known and the fix is a deletion; the plan mostly decides how to prove it.

session.summary: Plan v1.0.2 has two phases: remove the self-test, then add a test that fails if a life is ever lost without a hit.

sections.heading: Phases
items: 1. Remove the self-test and its constants from src/hazards.js, and add the no-loss-without-hit test.
2. Update the changelog and release v1.0.2.

sections.heading: Definition of done
items: Across 500 seeded runs of 20,000 ticks, every life lost has a matching hit.
